title: Three kinds of caller, one set of rules: every path ends in the same services
aria: Three kinds of caller reach Billpod's services. The screens call REST routes, which call the services directly. The in-app assistant and outside assistants over MCP both hand tool calls to one runner, which runs one of 50 tools, and each tool calls the same services. A rate limit kept on one REST route had to be copied into a tool by hand. A parity test checks that every route has a tool or a written reason.

build.title: Who asks
build.text: Three kinds of caller: a person on the app's screens, a person in the app's own chat, and an outside assistant such as Claude or ChatGPT.

build.title: Where each one comes in
build.text: The screens call REST routes. The chat goes to Ask Billpod, where Gemini picks a tool. Outside assistants call the MCP endpoint with an OAuth token. Each entry point keeps only its own rules, such as Ask Billpod's card.

build.title: One tool layer for both AI callers
build.text: Ask Billpod and `/mcp` hand every tool call to `runTool`. It checks the scopes and the input, then runs one of 50 tools, each defined once.

build.title: Every path ends in the same services
build.text: The tools call the same service functions as the REST routes. The rules live there, so all three callers obey them.

build.title: A rule kept in one entry point
build.text: The upload limit sits on a REST route, so Billpod had to copy it into a tool by hand. A parity test fails when a new route has neither a tool nor a written reason.

route.title: The app's chat builds the caller's context
route.text: A person tells Ask Billpod, the app's own assistant, that they paid the electricity bill. Before any tool runs, Ask Billpod builds one context: who asks, which household, which permissions (scopes), and that the caller is the assistant.

route.title: A card before any change
route.text: Gemini picks `mark_paid` from the 46 tools Ask Billpod offers. `mark_paid` is on the confirm list of 31 tools, so nothing runs yet. The person sees a card built from the stored bill and presses Approve.

route.title: The approved call goes into the one runner
route.text: Every AI entry point hands its calls to `runTool`. It checks the scopes and the input against the tool's schema, then runs `mark_paid`'s handler.

route.title: The handler calls the service the Pay button calls
route.text: The handler calls `bills.pay`, the same function the screen's REST route calls. The rules live there: the household filter and "already paid". The bill is now paid.

route.title: An hour later, Claude calls the same tool
route.text: The person forgot and asks Claude to pay the bill. Claude runs its own model and calls `mark_paid` over MCP with an access token. `/mcp` builds the same kind of context. Only the scopes and the caller differ.

route.title: Here the confirmation is Claude's choice
route.text: Billpod draws no card inside Claude. `mark_paid` carries `destructiveHint: true`, so Claude decides whether to ask first. The scopes, the input check and the service's rules still apply.

route.title: Same runner, same service, same refusal
route.text: The call goes through the same `runTool` to the same `bills.pay`, and the service refuses: "This bill is already paid." Claude gets it back as `isError: true`. The Pay button would get the same answer.
